entries.source: SDK 26.2, MPVolumeView.h, @property (nonatomic, strong, nullable) UIImage *volumeWarningSliderImage MP_API(ios(7.0))
entries.reason: read CLASS-SCOPED with tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua over the armv7 cache of 6.1.3, MPVolumeView is PRESENT with 54 own instance methods and 0 own class methods, and neither -volumeWarningSliderImage nor -setVolumeWarningSliderImage: is among the 54; across all 11378 classes of the whole 6.1.3 cache exactly zero declare -volumeWarningSliderImage, so no category in any framework supplies it either. WHY THIS ROW IS IMPLEMENTED AND THE TWO MPVolumeView ROWS BESIDE IT STAY ABSENT is the distinction this row turns on: those two need a STATE that does not exist on this release - the route state behind the AirPlay UI is MPAudioDeviceController's private tables and no public API on 6.1.3 reads it, and AVAudioSession reports the AUDIO route, which would be a different API's answer under that property's name. This one is a readwrite image THE CALLER SUPPLIES, so there is nothing to discover and nothing to invent: what to store is the caller's own UIImage. IT IS NOT INERT, and the release's own surface is what shows the difference: -setVolumeThumbImage:forState: and -volumeThumbImageForState: are among the 54, which is how a caller already customises the image on this release's volume slider, so the value is stored on a view whose slider machinery is already equipped to hold one. What this does NOT claim is that the release draws it automatically - nothing in the 54 reads a property of that name, because the property IS the 7.0 one and the release predates it. THE VALUE IS AN ASSOCIATED OBJECT BECAUSE A CATEGORY CANNOT HAVE AN IVAR: the first draft synthesised one and clang answered '@synthesize not allowed in a category's implementation' plus two undeclared-identifier errors, and a subclass would claim a class the release already owns. This is the tree's own idiom - UIKit/CADisplayLink+FrameRate.m stores its two values the same way, with a static const char key and OBJC_ASSOCIATION_RETAIN_NONATOMIC - and RETAIN rather than COPY because a UIImage is immutable by contract and a copy would be a second object the release's drawing code would not recognise as the one the caller supplied
entries.effect: what the caller sets reads back as the SAME UIImage, retained for as long as the view holds it, and nil for a view nobody set - which is the header's own nullable and the normal state rather than an error. The image is stored; drawing it is the release's own thumb accessors' job and this row does not claim otherwise
